pos.personaBrief: Ceni promised an offensive Flamengo that presses high and likes possession (DOL 2020-11-10), with a proactive, Jorge Jesus-like side, not a counter-attacking one.

pro.personaBrief: He wanted better ball exit from the back (Correio Braziliense) and a team that wins the ball high and creates chances quickly (Goal), so patient build-up with vertical intent.

est.personaBrief: Flamengo had a defined 3-4-3 with the ball and a back four without it, with wingers and forwards rotating and moving across lines.

lar.personaBrief: Isla and Bruno Henrique opened wide to give width, Gabigol and BH opened on the flanks, wingers tracked back to the full-back, so the team used wide play.

blo.personaBrief: The team pressed the opponent's build-up and won balls in the attacking third (Goal 2020-11-12), taking Jorge Jesus concepts and a high line.

mar.personaBrief: No source on marking; he sees defensive errors as system errors, which leans to zonal organisation and spatial defending.

pla.personaBrief: He stressed following Flamengo's own offensive style and adapting to the players available, though he adjusts in some matches (three centre-backs, 2021-05).

res.personaBrief: He promised offensive football and played to attack, but was pragmatic about results at a big club under pressure.

sis.personaBrief: He attributed errors to the system and demanded defensive duties from all, as Isla, Arao and Filipe Luis rotated roles, while using stars like Gabigol and Diego within structure.

jog.personaBrief: He started the 36-year-old Diego as the classic 10, wanted quality passing from the back, and demanded pressing intensity.

bas.personaBrief: He asked for Muniz back from loan and used academy kids, but relied on veterans like Diego and Filipe Luis in a title-chasing, signing-heavy squad.

lid.personaBrief: He was a hands-on demanding coach, likened to Simeone, but said he does not command everything and relied on dialogue with the squad.
